newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's Labour promises new economic climate.
newsitem.headline: Malta's Labour promises new economic climate.

text.p: Maltese opposition leader Alfred Sant said on Thursday that his Labour Party would give Malta a new economic climate if it is elected to government.
He told a delegation from the powerful General Workers' Union that a Labour government would "instill renewed confidence in the country."
He promised a Labour government would remove VAT, reducing uncertainty in areas such as tourism, which saw a 10 percent drop in arrivals in the first five months of this year.
Sant said a Labour government would give priority to fighting inflation, currently running close to four percent, while the removal of VAT would increase purchasing power.

He reiterated his party's opposition to Maltese membership of the European Union, saying that, although Malta should have close relations with the union, its regulations were not suited for a small island state like Malta.

Malta applied for European Union membership in July 1989 and has been promised membership talks six months after the end of the current inter-governmental conference. The General Workers Union is also against EU membership.
VAT was introduced in January last year, but Labour has vowed to replace it with a system of customs duties, which were in place before the tax was introduced.

The Nationalist (Christian Democratic) government of prime minister Eddie Fenech Adami, in power since 1987, has insisted that Labour would not be able to recover revenue generated by VAT unless it introduced some other form of tax. But Sant had told supporters that, rather than increase taxes, a government led by him would cut spending. He has not specified where he would cut spending, but said it would not be in social welfare. Elections are due in Malta by the middle of next year.
